userStories.title: specSource/derivedFrom schema + hand-rolled validators
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need the issue schema and the hand-rolled validators to recognize specSource (grill|derived|operator) and derivedFrom so a stage:specified issue can declare it reached plan-readiness without a grill, with the discriminator's invariants enforced as data.
acceptanceCriteria: issues.schema.json adds `specSource` (enum "grill"|"derived"|"operator") and `derivedFrom` (array of string). An if/then conditional REQUIRES specSource when stage==="specified"; another REQUIRES derivedFrom with minItems>=1 when specSource==="derived"; another REQUIRES non-empty description when specSource is "derived" or "operator". An absent specSource on a pre-existing specified issue is tolerated by the validator (treated as "grill"). Smoke: grep -q 'specSource' confirms the string is present. [oracle: grep -q 'specSource' /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/scripts/cam/issues.schema.json]

The BINDING oracle for the schema-shape correctness is a schema-validation test in test/issues/spec.test.ts that exercises each if/then conditional (specSource-required-on-specified; derivedFrom-required-when-derived; description-required-when-derived-or-operator) AND the absent-specSource-treated-as-grill back-compat, not merely the grep smoke check. [oracle: bun test test/issues/spec.test.ts]

src/issues/types.ts adds `specSource?: "grill"|"derived"|"operator"` and `derivedFrom?: string[]` to IssueEntry. [oracle: grep -q 'specSource' /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/src/issues/types.ts]

src/issues/spec.ts gains a hand-rolled validator (mirroring validateSpec/validateWsjf style, returning {ok, errors}) that enforces the 4 invariants: specSource-required-on-specified (absent⟹grill back-compat), specSource is one of the 3 enum values, derivedFrom non-empty when specSource==="derived" (and absent/empty otherwise), description non-empty when specSource in {derived, operator}. [oracle: bun test test/issues/spec.test.ts]

Option Y invariant: the 3 plannability filter sites keep the `stage === "specified"` predicate UNCHANGED (Option Y redefines the MEANING of specified, never the predicate) at src/issues/select.ts:34 (`issue.stage === "specified" &&`), src/issues/rank.ts:154 (`(issue) => issue.stage === "specified" && issue.status === "open",`), and src/issues/gate.ts:150 (`backlog.filter((e) => e.stage === "specified" && e.status === "open").map((e) => e.id),`); this story does not modify those files. [oracle: git diff --quiet src/issues/select.ts src/issues/rank.ts src/issues/gate.ts (no change to the three predicate sites)]

Unit tests cover: each invariant pass and fail case; absent-specSource-on-specified treated as grill (passes); specSource==="derived" without derivedFrom fails; specSource==="operator" with empty description fails; a valid grill/derived/operator entry each passes. [oracle: bun test test/issues/spec.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
The full spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: scripts/cam/issues.schema.json (draft-07, additionalProperties:false at root, uses required+enum), src/issues/types.ts (IssueEntry), src/issues/spec.ts (mirror validateSpec/validateWsjf shape: ValidationResult {ok, errors}), test/issues/spec.test.ts. PROJECT HAND-ROLLS validation, no ajv: the schema is data (used for docs + as the JSON-schema if/then guardrail layer), the TS validator is the runtime gate. Both layers must encode the same 4 invariants (gotcha: keep them in sync, do not let the schema and the validator drift). noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard array/optional access. specSource is a TOTAL discriminator with absent⟹grill (settled, gotcha #1). derivedFrom is string[] (a fix can consolidate several parents, gotcha #3). HARD MUST-NOT (operator-flagged): do NOT touch the plannability predicate at select.ts:34 / rank.ts:154 / gate.ts:150 — Option Y changes only the meaning of specified.

userStories.title: Filing flags --fast-track / --derived-from with hard guardrails + WSJF resolution
userStories.description: As an orchestrator filing a derived fix or an operator nice-to-have, I need `cam issue --file-local --fast-track` and `--derived-from CAM-NNN[,CAM-MMM]` to file the issue directly at stage:specified with the right specSource/derivedFrom, resolving WSJF (explicit or parent-inherited) and refusing pre-commit when any guardrail is violated, so born-ready work reaches /cam-plan without ceremony but cannot become a rigor shortcut.
acceptanceCriteria: parseIssueArgs (index.ts) accepts `--fast-track` and `--derived-from CAM-NNN[,CAM-MMM]` on the --file-local path; `--fast-track`⟹specSource:operator, `--derived-from`⟹specSource:derived with derivedFrom parsed from the comma-separated list; default filing with NO flag stays stage:idea (alloc.ts:95 default untouched). [oracle: bun test test/issue-dispatch.test.ts]

writeIssueFile (src/issues/alloc.ts) accepts specSource/derivedFrom/wsjf options and, when filing fast-track, sets stage:'specified' and writes specSource + derivedFrom into the IssueEntry, then syncs the worktree post-CAS (CAM-142 syncWorktreeIfOnMain path preserved, no staged-deletion). [oracle: bun test test/issues/alloc.test.ts]

WSJF is resolved at filing: explicit scores on stdin are accepted; with --derived-from and omitted scores, a SUGGESTED (overridable) WSJF is inherited from the parent issue read from main; filing REFUSES with a clear error message and non-zero exit when WSJF is unresolvable (no explicit scores AND no parent-with-wsjf). [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]

All 4 guardrails are enforced HARD pre-commit in createLocalIssueOnMain (src/commands/issue-file.ts), mirroring specifyIssueOnMain's validate-before-mutate order: specSource-required, derivedFrom-when-derived, description-non-empty-when-fast-track, WSJF-resolvable. A violation returns a non-ok outcome (no commit), printError fires, dispatch exits non-zero. [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]

Refusal tests prove: --derived-from naming a parent that has no wsjf and no explicit scores REFUSES (non-zero, no commit); --fast-track with empty description REFUSES; a valid --fast-track files at stage:specified with specSource:operator; a valid --derived-from inherits parent wsjf and files at stage:specified with specSource:derived + derivedFrom. [oracle: bun test test/issue-file.test.ts]

Boundary: fast-track is set ONLY via the explicit --fast-track / --derived-from flags (no content-heuristic auto-marking); the reviewer-SUGGESTION auto-filer is explicitly OUT of scope (separate follow-up issue that consumes this fast-track). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
The full spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: index.ts (parseIssueArgs ParsedIssueArgs union ~L605, dispatchIssue ~L1161, _buildCreateIssueOpts ~L1134 — the stdin payload + flags must thread through), src/commands/issue-file.ts (createLocalIssueOnMain: add guardrail validation before writeIssueFile, mirror checkMainUpToDate→validate→mutate order; read parent issue for WSJF inheritance via readBacklogFromMain), src/issues/alloc.ts (writeIssueFile WriteIssueFileOptions: add specSource/derivedFrom/wsjf, set stage when fast-track), test/issue-dispatch.test.ts (argv parse — gotcha: argv-shape tests do NOT prove tmux semantics, but this is the in-process --file-local path so injectable fakes are fine), test/issue-file.test.ts, test/issues/alloc.test.ts. Gotcha #2: WSJF inheritance is a SUGGESTED DEFAULT (overridable), NOT a binding copy — a derived fix can be more time-critical than its parent (CAM-143 footgun vs CAM-142 feature). Gotcha #4: writeIssueFile is the CAM-90 CAS primitive; since CAM-142 it syncs the worktree after CAS, do not regress that. Reuse the US-001 validator for the hard pre-commit guardrail. The ranker missing-wsjf sort-last+warning (src/issues/rank.ts computeWsjf) stays as a legacy/integrity net only — do NOT make it the designed WSJF path. No content-heuristic auto-marking; explicit flags only (spec criterion #8).

userStories.title: /cam-plan spec-sourcing by specSource + honest non-grilled signal
userStories.description: As the orchestrator running /cam-plan, I need the command to source the spec by specSource (grill ⟹ use the settled spec field do-not-re-litigate; derived/operator ⟹ use title+description as proposed scope and pass derivedFrom to the planner), and to print an honest non-grilled signal in place of the now-moot stage:idea D2 warning, so fast-tracked issues plan correctly while the grilled-spec contract stays intact.
acceptanceCriteria: .claude/commands/cam-plan.md sources the spec by specSource: "grill" (or absent, back-compat) ⟹ use the `spec` field as settled (do-not-re-litigate contract intact); "derived"/"operator" ⟹ use title+description as proposed scope (WHAT settled, HOW refined by planner); derivedFrom is passed to subagent-planner which reads the parent issue(s) for context; the auditor Step 8 backstop is described as unchanged. Smoke: grep -q 'specSource'; binding correctness is the embed/template parity test below. [oracle: grep -q 'specSource' /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/.claude/commands/cam-plan.md]

The stage:idea D2 warning (cam-plan.md:82) is replaced by an honest non-grilled signal for derived/operator specs, e.g. "non-grilled spec (specSource: derived, from CAM-NNN); treating description as proposed scope". [oracle: grep -q 'non-grilled' /Users/eduardo/Documents/Projects/cam-cli/.claude/commands/cam-plan.md]

templates/commands/cam-plan.md receives the matching spec-sourcing + non-grilled-signal change, preserving the existing intentional .claude-vs-template wording deltas (the project's dual-copy is per-file, not byte-identical). subagent-planner instructions (.claude/agents/subagent-planner.md + templates/agents/subagent-planner.md) document that derivedFrom parent issue(s) must be read for context when specSource is derived. Vendor drift check passes after re-embedding (bun run embed-vendor then bun run embed-vendor:check): src/vendor/_generated.ts reflects the edited cam-plan.md + subagent-planner.md copies (this is the binding oracle for the doc changes, not the single-token greps above). userStories.notes: Files: .claude/commands/cam-plan.md (D2 warning at line 82; the 'none' issue-source step), templates/commands/cam-plan.md, .claude/agents/subagent-planner.md, templates/agents/subagent-planner.md, src/vendor/_generated.ts (REGENERATED, never hand-edited — run `bun run embed-vendor`). Gotcha: cam dual-copy is per-file, NOT uniformly byte-identical (.claude vs templates have intentional wording deltas like 'bun run typecheck' vs 'the project's typecheck command'); diff before editing, edit BOTH copies, do not collapse the deltas. test/embedded.test.ts asserts codegen byte-parity for both EMBEDDED_CONTENTS and templatesContents — it WILL fail if _generated.ts is stale, so re-run embed-vendor after editing any shipped artifact. The grilled-spec 'do not re-litigate' contract for specSource:grill must stay verbatim. This story touches templates/ ⟹ embed-vendor:check is mandatory.

userStories.title: ADR documenting the two-door plan-readiness decision
userStories.description: As a future cam maintainer, I need an ADR in docs/adr/ recording that plan-readiness now has two doors (grilled OR born-ready), revising the CAM-107 'grill is the singular human gate' decision, with the alternatives and consequences captured, so the surprising redefinition of stage:specified is explained with its trade-offs.
acceptanceCriteria: A new ADR file under docs/adr/ (e.g. docs/adr/0002-fast-track-plan-ready.md) documents the decision per the 3-gate ADR convention in scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md: it states the decision (Option Y: file-as-specified with a specSource discriminator), the context (revises ADR 0001 / CAM-107 'grill is the singular human gate'; PRD-readiness now has two doors), the alternatives considered (X grillExempt-flag-stays-idea vs Y file-as-specified; binding vs overridable WSJF inheritance; soft vs hard guardrails), and the consequences (speed for derived work, rigor-skip mitigated by hard guardrails + auditor backstop + explicit-only marking). [oracle: file-assert test in test/ greps the new ADR for the required section headings (Decisao/Decision, Contexto/Context, Alternativas/Alternatives, Consequencias/Consequences) and the strings 'CAM-107' and 'specSource']

The ADR prose contains no em-dash and no decorative emoji (project doc convention; use colon/comma/parenthesis/period instead). [oracle: file-assert grep -L for the em-dash character in the new ADR file]
